value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Real reference evidence: TS 2026.10.5 and native have byte-identical combined-cap failures (50-row snapshot hashed after amount cap, unchanged replay stale; producer limit 50/output limit 30 rebases using capped count and skips rows after deletion). Preserving pinned parity is the default pending user steering. Float divergence confirmed with metadata 1e20: native prints exponent form, TS prints decimal; row counts and snapshot hashes differ, and native rejects the TS cursor as stale. 30.0 itself is normalized to integer by current TOON decoding, so regression also includes actual surviving float metadata. Equals-form controls also differ in refusal receipts. Number formatting must be shared across hashes, wire JSON and token estimates to fix the full float envelope.

Prior differential evidence is confirmed against the installed TS 2026.10.5: findings 4182703846 and 4182703859 reproduce byte-identically in the published reference (snapshot hashed after the amount cap with stale unchanged replay; producer rebasing uses the capped count after deletion), so they are pinned as reference parity with new differential tests rather than diverging fixes. 4182703871 and 4182703906 are real divergences: shared JS-compatible number formatting (ryu-js) now covers history hashes, snapshot hashes, wire JSON and token estimates, and equals-form native controls are stripped from recovery. Re-verified against the real TS CLI: float values match byte-for-byte (30.0 as 30, 1e20 as 100000000000000000000, 1e-6 as 0.000001). Also confirmed native sorts extra metadata keys while the reference preserves file order — a pre-existing separate divergence that will be filed as a follow-up item, out of this slice.

value.text: Coverage-gate follow-up: the first instrumented run of the JS number-formatting fix reported one uncovered region in the CLI response writer. Root cause: the to_value error region of the generic writer could only be exercised by a synthetic test-only serialization type, and the region summary never counted that record. The response writer now serializes through a shared JavaScript-number formatter (serde_json Serializer with a custom Formatter; pretty layout identical to the reference), which restores the original writer-error topology and removes the to_value intermediate entirely. A wire-bytes equivalence test asserts the writer's output equals the shared renderer plus newline. Instrumented aggregate now reports 100 percent on all four metrics: 3036/3036 lines, 273/273 functions, 4605/4605 regions, 624/624 branches, with all 197 tests passing including the byte-exact differential suite.

value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Finding 4184061254 reproduced against published PM CLI 2026.10.5; the installed 2026.10.6 context-intent decoder is identical. A 75-item triage page with limit 69 produced a producer cursor at after_index 68. Stripping after_index and requesting the final page with --for triage --token-budget 800 --full made native compact three rows and write after_index 3. The reference omitted the page with budget_exceeded effective_budget_infeasible and did not rebase. Deleting the rebased identity then resumed at demo-0015 and repeated earlier rows. Native now requires after_index before compaction, matching the reference omission. The unit regression legacy_final_page_without_after_index_does_not_rebase_from_zero fails when that requirement is removed. The differential legacy_after_without_after_index_omits_final_triage_page pins the published omission. No upstream issue: the reference does not rebase from zero. The remaining continuation_contract.fingerprint gap is tracked in pm-rust-poen and is not changed in this slice.

value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Finding 4184061258: cursor refusals read std::env::args_os and lossily own each argument, so a non-UTF-8 argument cannot panic the JSON refusal. The envelope still exits 2. Unix unit test non_utf8_arguments_publish_the_cursor_refusal_envelope publishes a non-UTF-8 OsString inside that envelope. Process test non_utf8_workspace_argument_refuses_a_bad_cursor_without_panic exits 2; reverting the call site to env::args panics with exit 101 and fails that test. Windows CI does not construct invalid OsStrings. Local just release-check passed after the decode-failure coverage fix: formatting, deny-warning clippy, private and public rustdoc, full suite, 100 percent lines functions regions and branches (3046/3046, 274/274, 4616/4616, 624/624), cargo audit, and pinned changelog check.
